purpose: Verified problems, root causes, and permanent fixes. Load at session start; apply all fixes automatically before generating. Never reintroduce a solved problem.

fixes.problem: LR-0135 (2026-07-15): across multiple studio renders (with the rescaled/repositioned logo already fixed for size), the printed logo showed fuzzy/vector-sharp-inconsistent edges, uneven line thickness, a bright WHITE HALO/glow patch on the cloth directly behind the logo separating it from the fabric, evenly-bright gold that ignores the cloth's directional lighting, and no visible weave/fold distortion through the ink - reads as an AI-painted graphic pasted on top, not ink printed into the fabric during the same photoshoot. User: this is exactly what makes AI catalog images look artificial.
fixes.root_cause: the model renders the logo as a separate bright asset composited onto the cloth (adding contrast via a light halo to make it legible) instead of treating it as ink absorbed into the same material already lit by the scene.
fixes.fix: LOGO PHYSICAL PRINT RULE (CRITICAL, every studio prompt): the logo is REAL GOLD INK PRINTED DIRECTLY onto the cloth - never redraw/regenerate/repaint/restyle/vectorize/recreate it, and never place ANY shadow, glow, white patch, blur, gradient, halo, emboss effect, lighting effect, reflection, drop shadow, or artificial background/masking beneath or around it. Only the gold ink itself should be visible - the cloth texture continues naturally underneath with no visible masking/background layer, and the logo casts no shadow of its own. The logo must inherit the cloth's texture (weave visible through the ink), folds (ink bends/distorts over folds), perspective, lighting direction and shadows, and surface imperfections - same lighting calibration as the rest of the cloth, not evenly bright regardless of scene light. BLOCKING VALIDATION: if any shadow, glow, white background, masking, halo, or AI-generated separation-effect appears around the logo, the render is INVALID - discard and regenerate.

fixes.problem: LR-0135 (2026-07-15): a studio render showed a section of the continuous eternity band DETACHED and standing upright with no mechanical support - an impossible floating diamond segment, as if the band had a hinge/opening mechanism the real product does not have. The detached section also changed the spacing/alignment/geometry of the emerald-cut stones. User classified this as 'AI concept render / fantasy composite jewelry artwork / not a real product photograph' and 'complete rejection' - would misrepresent the product in an Etsy listing.
fixes.root_cause: the model treated the source as loose creative inspiration rather than a single rigid manufactured object, inventing an artistic/impossible construction (opening, hinge, floating segment) instead of photographing the one real physical ring.
fixes.fix: NO PRODUCT MODIFICATION RULE (CRITICAL, every prompt): the ring is a finished manufactured product and a SINGLE CONTINUOUS PHYSICAL OBJECT. Never add moving parts, hinges, openings, detached sections, floating diamonds, exploded/cutaway views, or artistic effects. Never separate any portion of the band. Never make any diamond float independent of the band. Never invent a product configuration that could not physically exist. Only photograph the actual uploaded ring exactly as it exists - camera/background/lighting/pose may change, the physical construction may never change. BLOCKING VALIDATION: if any part of the jewelry appears detached, floating, bent, opened, or mechanically altered vs. a single rigid band, the render is INVALID - discard and regenerate before delivery.

fixes.problem: LR-0135 (2026-07-15): a lifestyle shot (hand raised near face) rendered the ring 3-5x too large relative to the fingers, floating with no finger penetration, inside of the band fully visible, no contact shadows/skin compression/occlusion, and mismatched camera perspective/DoF/lighting between the ring and the hand - reads as a catalog PNG pasted onto a hand photo, not a real worn photograph. User: 'complete rejection for an Etsy listing.'
fixes.root_cause: pose-reference-driven generation (lifestyle/closeup, only 2 medias: pose + source) inserts the source ring into the scene as an overlay rather than integrating it as a physically worn object at real-world scale - same pose-reference-dominance root cause family as uniform-eternity-band-graduated-drift, emerald-cut-orientation-lock, and lifestyle-prong-and-bezel-drift.
fixes.observed_failure_2026-07-16: OPPOSITE scale direction confirms the same failure: round-halo twist-shank SKU lifestyle shot rendered the ring TOO SMALL / thin / dainty on the hand - head-to-band proportion compressed, large double-infinity twist shoulders reduced to thin partial curves, pave stripped from the loop strands, band much thinner, AND the center stone shape changed (round brilliant -> oval/cushion-ish, smaller). User: 'complete rejection - the output is a different ring design.' Lock BOTH directions: the worn ring is never enlarged NOR shrunk/daintied; head size, shoulder mass, band width and the center-stone SHAPE (round stays round) are held at source proportions - lifestyle changes only hand/environment/camera/lighting/DoF.
fixes.fix: LIFESTYLE PRODUCT INTEGRITY (CRITICAL, every lifestyle/closeup prompt): never overlay/paste/composite/scale the source ring onto the scene as a flat asset. The ring must be worn naturally - the finger passes THROUGH the inside of the band (inner band NOT fully visible), correct occlusion, natural contact shadows where metal meets skin, slight skin compression, and the ring at its exact REAL-WORLD size relative to the finger (never enlarged AND never shrunk/daintied to look more 'natural' or more 'visible'). NEVER simplify the infinity/twist shoulders, reduce the head size, thin the band, remove pave stones, or change the center-stone shape (round stays round, oval stays oval) - those are the same geometry-lock features as studio, held identically in worn shots. Camera perspective, depth of field, lighting direction and focus must MATCH between the ring and the hand - no compositing mismatch. Final result must read as a real photograph of a person wearing the actual manufactured ring at its true manufactured size, never a pasted/composited render and never a slimmed-down 'daintier' reinterpretation.

fixes.problem: LR-0135 (2026-07-15): source ring = emerald-cut diamonds VERTICALLY oriented (portrait) with each stone's long axis running AROUND the band's circumference. Multiple lifestyle renders rotated every stone 90 degrees to landscape (long axis running ACROSS the band width instead) - confirmed on 2+ separate lifestyle shots (marble surface, near-face). User: 'this isn't a lighting/perspective issue - it's a geometry reconstruction error, the AI recreated the ring instead of faithfully photographing it,' and it 'changes the ring's visual design, makes it a different product.'
fixes.root_cause: pose-reference-driven shots (lifestyle/closeup, only 2 medias: pose + source) let the model re-orient stones to whatever reads as 'natural' for the hand angle instead of preserving the source's exact rotational angle per stone; same root cause family as uniform-eternity-band-graduated-drift and lifestyle-prong-and-bezel-drift (pose reference outweighs source fidelity).
fixes.fix: ABSOLUTE PRODUCT GEOMETRY LOCK, BLOCKING VALIDATION (user-locked 2026-07-15): diamond orientation/rotation/dimensions/placement/spacing/count, prong position/geometry, band width/thickness, gallery structure, finger coverage are ALL permanently locked - never redesign/reinterpret/reconstruct/optimize any part of the jewelry, only camera/background/lighting/pose may change. For emerald-cut stones specifically: the long axis of every stone MUST remain exactly as in the source - this SKU's source is VERTICAL (portrait), long axis running AROUND the band circumference - every generated image must preserve that exact vertical orientation; never rotate any stone by any amount; never convert portrait->landscape or landscape->portrait. Every prompt (studio AND lifestyle AND closeup) must state this explicitly, not rely on the generic DESIGN STRING. TREAT AS A BLOCKING QC GATE: if stone orientation changes from vertical to horizontal (or vice versa) vs the source, the render is INVALID - discard and regenerate before it can be delivered or approved, same severity as a wrong prong count.

fixes.problem: LR-0135 (2026-07-15): source is a UNIFORM eternity band (all emerald/baguette-cut diamonds the SAME size, same shape, evenly spaced all the way around, no single dominant stone). Studio shots (source+branded-cloth+logo medias) rendered this correctly. But ALL lifestyle and close-up shots (source+pose-reference medias, no logo) drifted it into a completely different architecture: a large dominant 'center' stone flanked by 3 smaller stones stepping down in size on each side (a graduated three/five-stone anniversary-band look) - user called this 'complete rejection', flagged changed diamond position, changed diamond size, changed ring size.
fixes.root_cause: the lifestyle/closeup pose reference dominates when the source pattern is a repetitive/uniform band; the model falls back to the far more common 'graduated center-stone' ring trope instead of reproducing a flat, uniform, repeating diamond sequence - same failure family as lifestyle-prong-and-bezel-drift (pose reference treated as inspiration, not the source treated as ground truth).
fixes.fix: For ANY uniform/eternity/repeating-pattern band (no single larger center stone), the lifestyle and close-up prompts must explicitly state: 'UNIFORM ETERNITY BAND - every diamond around the ENTIRE band is the SAME size, SAME shape, SAME cut, evenly spaced with identical gaps; there is NO larger center stone and NO graduated/stepped-down sizing; never render this as a three-stone/five-stone/graduated-center design; the band reads identically whether viewed from any point around its circumference.' State this with the SAME strength as the studio prompt's geometry lock - do not rely on the generic DESIGN STRING alone for lifestyle/closeup; pose-reference-driven shots need the uniform-pattern constraint spelled out explicitly every time, since the failure is specific to those two shot types and did not occur on studio.

fixes.problem: AI generation drifts jewelry geometry (head, halo outer diameter + rim thickness, center-stone diameter + center-to-halo ratio, 4-prong positions/angles/size, halo stone count/spacing/diameter, shank width/thickness, shoulder->head transition, cathedral/gallery architecture, basket/support-bar design, twist/crossover/braided-shank geometry + its open negative spaces, pave routing/spacing, side profile/curvature/height, metal thickness, stone proportions, silhouette). User requires a 100% geometry match, which nano_banana cannot guarantee. Never ship a redesigned ring; never ask the user which fallback to use.
fixes.observed_failure_2026-07-16: twist-halo split-shank SKU: output was visually attractive but an 'inspired recreation', not the same ring. Drifted: (1) twist crossover softened/flattened, negative spaces closed, intersections differ; (2) halo thicker + merged into the head vs thin halo sitting higher above the gallery; (3) gallery/basket redesigned into a different mounting; (4) band thicker, heavier proportions; (5) pave routing + stone spacing off the twist path; (6) side silhouette/height/curvature changed; (7) head/crown height + viewing angle inconsistent. Every structural feature = FAIL. This is the exact case the auto-fallback exists for: do NOT ship the redesign - composite the real source-ring pixels (FALLBACK 1) or render the angle from CAD (FALLBACK 2).
fixes.observed_failure_2026-07-16_b: SECOND SKU (round-halo twist-shank studio shot) same redesign failure, confirming the pattern: halo thicker + halo diamonds larger so the halo dominates; center stone larger relative to the halo with different crown/table balance; twist shoulders widened + reshaped; pave larger + differently spaced (count/spacing off); prongs thicker + repositioned; overall head size/shoulder width/halo thickness/band thickness/pave spacing all drifted. GEOMETRY LOCK: only environment/background, lighting, camera angle, focus/DoF, shadows, reflections may change - all structure identical. Same physical ring moved to a new photoshoot, never a reinterpreted version (product-vs-lifestyle distinction: a lifestyle image = same ring, different setting, NOT a redesign). = FAIL -> auto-fallback, never ship.
fixes.observed_failure_2026-07-16_v_gallery: LR-0151-type round solitaire pave: source = open basket with curved support arms, NO gallery directly beneath the center stone, clean open side profile. LEGACY render INVENTED a triangular/V-shaped gallery + extra metal support under the stone, changed head/basket architecture ('no longer the same ring'). This is the head/gallery invention subtype (docs/16 HEAD & GALLERY LOCK): never fill/close open spaces, never invent a gallery/under-gallery/support arms. Occurred on the LEGACY path; composite-v1 (now default) makes it impossible (ring = source pixels).
fixes.root_cause: a diffusion model re-synthesizes the ring on every new camera angle; it recognizes 'twisted halo engagement ring' and generates a statistically similar ring rather than reproducing the exact CAD engineering. Sub-1% CAD fidelity is impossible by generation alone, so an 'auto-regenerate until identical' loop never converges and only burns credits - which is why the composite fallback is mandatory, not optional.
fixes.fix: PERMANENT AUTO-FALLBACK WORKFLOW (user-locked 2026-07-13; NEVER ask the user to choose - switch automatically): (1) ATTEMPT AI generation with the strict locked-geometry prompt - source images fed FIRST at max weight; only camera angle/position/lens/perspective/composition/cloth/background/lighting/reflections/shadows/DoF may change; never redesign/reinterpret/optimize/smooth/reconstruct the ring. (2) AUTO-QC every output vs the source images across: head; halo outer diameter + metal rim thickness; center-stone diameter + center-to-halo ratio; 4-prong positions/angles/size/orientation; halo diamond count/spacing/diameter + halo thickness/height above the gallery; shank width/thickness; shoulder-to-head transition; cathedral/gallery/basket architecture + support bars; twist/crossover/braided-shank geometry + its open negative spaces; pave routing/spacing along the shank; side profile/curvature/height; head/crown height + viewing angle; metal thickness everywhere; diamond proportions; every contour/silhouette. (3) If ANY geometry differs, DO NOT deliver. (4) AUTOMATICALLY switch to the next fallback without asking: FALLBACK 1 = preserve the ORIGINAL jewelry exactly and composite the real source-ring pixels into the AI-generated scene via scripts/composite_ring_into_scene.py, matching lighting/shadows/reflections/perspective/DoF/color; FALLBACK 2 = if compositing cannot achieve the requested camera angle, render the exact geometry at that angle from the original CAD model (only if the CAD file is available), then composite onto cloth. Never deliver a regenerated ring whose geometry changed. QC PASS BAR: 100% geometry match + natural macro photography + bright neutral-white daylight + physically realistic reflections + logo physically printed into the fabric + camera angles varied across catalogs + focus always on the jewelry.
fixes.prompt_level_prevention_2026-07-16: three SKUs drifted, so the GEOMETRY LOCK now leads the actual generation prompt: every prompt begins with the 'CRITICAL REQUIREMENT - GEOMETRY LOCK' header (prompts/07 canonical base prompt) BEFORE the angle/scene tag, because the model weights the prompt opening most. The consolidated spec + pre-accept QA checklist is docs/13_JEWELRY_PRESERVATION_SPEC.md - run that checklist against the source before accepting any image; any mismatch = FAIL -> auto-fallback. Prompt/QA reduce drift; the composite fallback is what guarantees fidelity.

fixes.problem: AI renders a fake/garbled logo (e.g. 'ELLYREID', gray/wrong font, missing elements)
fixes.root_cause: nano_banana cannot reproduce fine logo typography
fixes.fix: NEVER let AI render/approximate the logo. Use exact asset (local composite) or OMIT. Missing OK; incorrect NOT OK.

fixes.problem: logo drawn/altered by AI (inaccurate vs preserved asset); or cloth freely invented by AI
fixes.root_cause: model given freedom to generate brand surfaces
fixes.fix: NEVER AI-generate the logo OR the background cloth. Logo = exact preserved assets/logo/logo_official.png via local composite, or omit. Cloth = approved premium white cotton reproduced faithfully, never a new AI fabric.

fixes.problem: logo looks pasted/floating/flat on top of the cloth, not printed in
fixes.root_cause: overlay instead of print-into-fabric blend
fixes.fix: logo must read as metallic ink printed INTO the cloth (multiply-blend, texture shows through, follows weave/folds/light/shadow); a pasted look = FAIL, re-composite tuning --displace/--opacity/--scale/--pos

fixes.problem: cloth rendered yellowish/warm, or plain/flat/cheap and simple
fixes.root_cause: warm white balance / AI substituting a cheaper flat fabric
fixes.fix: cloth must be premium white COTTON with natural soft draping and fine grain, pure neutral white; never yellow/warm (fix with whiten_cloth.py, 0 credits), never flat/simple/blank

fixes.problem: AI applies color grading / warm-tone or creative white balance; image drifts to a pink/yellow/red/cream/beige/warm (or cool) cast vs the neutral source
fixes.root_cause: model auto-grades / shifts white balance for 'style'
fixes.fix: source is the master for ALL colors; preserve palette + neutral WB exactly, no grading/LUT/warm enhancement; no tint or warm/cool cast; keep lighting neutral (no added warmth/saturation/contrast/HDR); metal+diamonds keep natural color; cloth stays source neutral white. FINAL VALIDATION each image: colors/WB match source, no tint, neutral light, premium neutral-white cloth, natural jewelry → fix locally (whiten_cloth.py, 0 credits) or regenerate before returning. Color fidelity > artistic styling.

fixes.problem: need a hard reject gate for logo/cloth defects + safe cross-device caching
fixes.root_cause: defects slipped through without an explicit reject rule
fixes.fix: REJECT/redo if: logo differs from preserved asset, logo looks AI-generated, logo not merged naturally, cloth material changes, cloth yellowish/non-white, or cloth flat/cheap/artificial/simple. Logo+cloth are preserved ASSETS (never AI-generated). Cache/reuse across devices+sessions byte-preserving only; verify against manifest locked_asset_checksums; never alter quality/fidelity.

fixes.problem: center stone shows doubled/mirrored ghost facet mesh (worst on large worn angles)
fixes.root_cause: AI invents a kaleidoscope facet pattern
fixes.fix: one real single-table brilliant facet pattern identical to source; no doubling/CGI symmetry

fixes.problem: overexposed/glowing pure-white diamond, blown highlights, plastic/milky
fixes.root_cause: over-enhancement
fixes.fix: natural brilliance only; visible facets; no artificial whitening/sparkle; no solid white areas

fixes.problem: diamond looks AI-enhanced/CGI/plastic/glass, milky/cloudy, bloomed, washed-out, over-sharpened, or fake-sparkly rather than professionally photographed
fixes.root_cause: model stylizes/over-enhances the gem instead of matching real optics
fixes.fix: match reference optical quality: crystal-clear water-like transparency, razor-sharp facet definition, excellent light return, high bright/dark facet contrast, natural white brilliance, small fire only where physically correct, accurate crown/table/pavilion/girdle geometry, crisp per-facet reflections. No milky/cloudy/washed-out/glow/bloom/fake-sparkle/overexposure/over-sharpen/plastic/glass/CGI. Reads as real VVS/IF macro studio photo; brilliance never boosted artificially.

fixes.problem: pave/side stones become white dots/glass beads/blurry blobs
fixes.root_cause: small-stone under-rendering
fixes.fix: every side stone individually faceted, real light behaviour, exact count/size/spacing

fixes.problem: LR-0141 rendered 8-prong crown vs source 4 pointed claws
fixes.root_cause: AI redesigned the head
fixes.fix: lock EXACT prong count/shape/position from source in the prompt; treat any construction change as failure

fixes.problem: lifestyle shot placed hand on a laptop/desk
fixes.root_cause: wrong reference/theme

fixes.problem: cloth drifts cream/ivory/warm

fixes.problem: ring floats / impossible balance / cloth penetration
fixes.root_cause: no physical grounding
fixes.fix: real contact points, believable supporting fold, correct contact shadows; regenerate impossible poses

fixes.problem: AI redesigns/beautifies/simplifies jewelry geometry vs the reference (wrong halo diameter, prong count, split-shank/crossover geometry, component spacing)
fixes.root_cause: model treats the reference as inspiration, not the exact product
fixes.fix: reference = MASTER PRODUCT, exact reproduction. Preserve every component AND the relative distances between them (silhouette, proportions, head/gallery/basket, prongs count/position/shape/thickness, center+side stone size/count/spacing, halo diameter+geometry, crossover, split-shank, band width/thickness/curvature, shoulder, setting, metal coverage, placement). Every visible pixel = ground truth. Only change camera/environment/lighting/background/composition. Any component differs -> regenerate.

fixes.problem: gemstone proportions/outline/table/depth change between angles; AI reconstructs a different-looking stone per shot
fixes.root_cause: model re-estimates the gem geometry instead of reusing the exact stone
fixes.fix: gem = exact physical stone; preserve identical across ALL angles: shape, outline, length-to-width ratio, table size, crown height, pavilion depth, girdle thickness, culet position, symmetry, profile, silhouette, apparent size, orientation, optical proportions. Rotating the camera reveals the same stone from a new view (only facet light/brilliance changes per real optics); never modify proportions or create a new gem.

fixes.problem: side/angled views change the stone's profile — deepened pavilion, taller crown, or an oval rendered rounder/wider than the reference
fixes.root_cause: model re-guesses the cut profile per angle instead of foreshortening the one stone
fixes.fix: from any side angle keep the reference's exact side profile; never deepen pavilion, increase crown height, shorten/widen the outline, or make an oval appear rounder. Apparent proportions across front/30/45/60/side/rear = those of the ONE physical ring (length-to-width ratio + crown/pavilion profile constant; only real-perspective foreshortening changes).

fixes.problem: the 5 studio angles come out too similar — hero/45L/45R all near-front, so 3+ shots look like the same view
fixes.root_cause: model renders small yaw changes as near-identical front views
fixes.fix: the five studio shots must be VISIBLY different camera positions (>=30-40 deg yaw/pitch apart): hero straight-on at ring height; 45L yaw ~45 left + raised ~30-35; 45R yaw ~45 right + raised ~30-35; side true 90 deg at ring height (stone top not a face); three-quarter high ~60 top-down at ~30 yaw. If two read as the same angle -> regenerate the duplicate at the correct distinct position. Camera changes only; ring stays identical.

fixes.problem: side/band diamonds or the band get redesigned/resized/respaced, or accent stones render with worse optics than the center
fixes.root_cause: model treats accents/band as filler and re-invents them
fixes.fix: preserve EXACTLY every side/band diamond (shape,size,count,proportions,position,spacing,orientation,alignment,setting,prongs/beads,metal coverage) and the band (width,thickness,shoulder width,taper,curvature,cross-section,metal volume,polish,proportions). Never redesign/resize/replace/reinterpret. Side+band stones get the SAME center-grade optics (natural facets/junctions/scintillation/fire/contrast/transparency/depth; no glow/over-whitening/blur/plastic/painted highlights). Every diamond = real pro-photographed stone. Only camera/environment/lighting change.

fixes.problem: diamond cut anatomy/optics drift between angles; accents simplified/blurred or baguettes rendered as generic glass
fixes.root_cause: model re-generates the stone per view instead of revealing the one existing stone
fixes.fix: diamond geometry already exists in the reference; every view = same physical stone from another camera. Preserve full cut anatomy exactly (dimensions, L:W, table, crown angle+height, pavilion depth, girdle, culet, facet layout/count/proportions, star/bezel/upper+lower-girdle facets, pavilion mains, symmetry, polish, optical symmetry). Camera change never alters thickness/volume/silhouette/optical pattern; every angle keeps identical facet pattern/brilliance/scintillation/fire/contrast/transparency/light-return/depth (no invented reflections/facets/pavilion/crown, no fake sparkle/glow/overexposure/melted facets/blurry junctions/plastic). Side views never make the stone thinner/thicker/longer/shorter/flatter/deeper/wider/narrower; pavilion+crown+girdle stay consistent with front. Accents (side/baguette/pave/halo) get same macro-lens quality+exact geometry as center; never simplify/blur/replace-with-glass. IGI-grade from every angle.

fixes.problem: elongated oval center drifts toward round/cushion/pear across angles/scenes; tapered baguette side stones get reshaped/swapped/simplified
fixes.root_cause: model substitutes a more common shape when the cut is elongated or the accents are baguettes
fixes.fix: ELONGATED OVAL center stays a true elongated oval in EVERY view (front/side/30/45/60/top/rear/lifestyle/studio) - never round, cushion-like, pear-like, wider, shorter, deeper, flatter, thicker, or differently faceted; preserve oval outline, L:W ratio, table/crown/pavilion/girdle, facet pattern, optical symmetry, size, depth, orientation. TAPERED BAGUETTE side stones preserved exactly - shape, taper, size, length, width, facet structure, angle, placement, setting, metal border; never reshaped/swapped/simplified/blurred. Reference image 1 is the sole source of truth; only camera/scene/background/composition/natural-lighting change. Reject+regenerate if shape/prongs/sides/band/setting/proportions differ.

fixes.problem: diamonds render with a CZ/moissanite/glass/plastic/acrylic/crystal fake-gem look; or scene uses moody/dramatic/cinematic/blackish/warm-indoor lighting that darkens or tints the shot
fixes.root_cause: model substitutes a cheaper gem look or a stylized lighting mood
fixes.fix: every stone (center + side) = premium natural-looking lab-grown diamond; NEVER CZ/moissanite(over-dispersive rainbow)/glass/plastic/acrylic/artificial-crystal/CGI-gem. LIGHTING = neutral daylight / luxury studio, soft shadows, clean highlights, neutral white balance; NEVER yellow/orange/blue/blackish/dark/warm-indoor/cinematic/dramatic/moody. White fabric stays pure neutral white, gold natural yellow, diamonds colorless. Lighting may change by scene but keeps the reference's calibration.

fixes.problem: in worn/lifestyle shots the model multiplies prongs (4->6/8), rounds/shrinks the center stone, and INVENTS a milgrain/bezel rim border around the stone; band bulks up or thins, pave spacing changes; RECURRED WORSE on LR-0141 (2026-07-12): full round bezel/rim border invented AND the band's pave diamonds were entirely REMOVED (not just drifted) AND the band's cross-section/shape itself changed
fixes.root_cause: small ring in a hand scene -> pose reference dominates and the model treats the ring as inspiration, adding common setting cliches (extra claws, milgrain bezel) and, in worse cases, silently drops small accent stones + reshapes the shank when the hand pose foreshortens the band
fixes.fix: lock the exact prong COUNT+positions from source (e.g. LR-0141 = EXACTLY 4 slim claws at ~10/2/5/7; never 6/8, never double into 8 tips); NO milgrain, NO bezel, NO rim/under-bezel border around the stone unless in source; keep the center stone the same size/roundness; band must keep its EXACT source cross-section/profile/width/taper (never flatten/round/thicken/thin into a different shank shape) AND every pave diamond along the band at its source position/count/spacing — a plain/bare stretch of band where the source had pave = FAIL, same severity as an invented bezel. VERIFY prong count + band pave count + band shape all match source before returning; if any differs, reject+regenerate. Same-physical-ring: only camera/scene/pose/background change.

fixes.problem: generative model drifts geometry; sandbox cannot download Higgsfield CDN output to auto-verify (403 both ways), so failures reach the user
fixes.root_cause: CDN egress blocked; text prompts only bias, never guarantee, geometry
fixes.fix: Enforce via Drive read-back QC: user (or Higgsfield save-to-Drive) drops renders into LR_Verify_Inbox (Drive id 1idwSM7EvXY7MijTZr-5FQ5sZmCnIQaX0); Claude downloads each, views, and verifies vs source: prong count/placement/size/angle; center shape/proportions/orientation/facets; head/basket/gallery/cathedral/setting; halo/hidden-halo/bezel/milgrain added-or-removed; pave/baguette/side-stone layout; band width/thickness/taper/shank/metal geometry; metal color/finish/texture; overall geometry; LIGHTING = bright neutral daylight only, no warm/yellow/orange/blue/green/colored/moody/dramatic, consistent exposure, neutral WB, true-to-life. Auto-reject+regenerate any fail until 100% pass; if a shot cannot pass, FAIL it (report) rather than ship a redesigned ring. Deliver only verified passes. Ring = locked CAD model; only camera/pose/composition/background/DoF change.

fixes.problem: the ring is not instantly the focal point: eye is pulled to cloth/props/flowers/books/furniture/hands/scenery; background too busy or sharper than the ring; ring framed small with large empty negative space; wide environmental or portrait-style hand shots where the hand is the subject; OR (2026-07-15) ring placed off-center/near an edge instead of centered
fixes.root_cause: composition treats the scene/hand as the subject and the jewelry as one element among many, instead of the single hero
fixes.fix: SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-13 version (user-locked 2026-07-15: centered framing + 55-70% replaces off-center + 70-90%). Jewelry is ALWAYS the hero in every studio/lifestyle/closeup shot; the viewer's eye must land on the ring within the first second. The jewelry occupies 55-70% of visual attention; focus locks on the center stone + ring. POSITION: the ring is CENTERED horizontally and vertically, visually balanced, never placed near the edges. Frame the ring LARGE and prominent without cropping key design details (prongs/gallery/side stones/band) - never shrink it; keep balanced margins and comfortable breathing room. Background is support only: minimal, premium, softly blurred, with blur increasing away from the jewelry (real macro shallow DoF); background must NEVER be sharper than the ring. Camera priority: 1 jewelry, 2 diamond brilliance, 3 metal finish, 4 ring geometry, 5 background. Logo (studio shots) stays supporting space only, roughly consistent position shot-to-shot, never approaching the ring's dominance. In lifestyle shots the hand/skin is a STAND, not the subject - ring stays hero, framed large, NOT portrait-style hand photography. FORBIDDEN: busy backgrounds, distracting props, strong competing textures, large empty negative space, wide environmental shots, portrait framing with the hand as subject, background sharper than the ring, off-center/edge-placed jewelry, any composition where the jewelry is not instantly the focal point. Every shot must read as luxury jewelry product photography; if the eye goes anywhere but the ring first, the ring isn't centered, or the background competes/out-sharpens it -> regenerate.

fixes.problem: catalogs look templated, repetitive and AI-generated: the same fixed 5 camera setups every SKU, everything uniformly in focus, flat clinical lighting, waxy over-smooth surfaces — the shots read as artificial renders, not real photography
fixes.root_cause: reusing one canonical angle set for every catalog and defaulting to uniformly-sharp, clinically-even compositions that trigger the 'AI look'
fixes.fix: ROTATE the camera geometry per catalog — do NOT reuse the previous SKU's exact setups. §A's five roles still define coverage, but each catalog draws a DIFFERENT combination and includes 1-2 harder/dynamic angles (bird's-eye ~75-85° top-down; low near-table worm's-eye ~10-15°; over-the-shoulder three-quarter; raked oblique macro; gentle natural handheld tilt; profile at slight 10-15° yaw). Keep the five mutually distinct (≥ 30-40° separation). Make every frame read as REAL macro photography: genuine shallow depth of field with a real focal plane and soft falloff (not everything razor-sharp); CENTERED, visually balanced framing (user-locked 2026-07-15 — supersedes the earlier off-center/rule-of-thirds requirement; ring centered horizontally+vertically, never near an edge); organic gravity-driven cloth folds; real-lens character (edge falloff, believable speculars, soft shadow gradients, faint natural imperfection); avoid remaining AI tells = unnaturally even lighting, all-in-focus, plastic/waxy surfaces. Bright neutral-white daylight and byte-identical ring geometry are unchanged — this varies only camera craft, never centering/composition-balance. If a shot looks artificial/rendered → regenerate with a more natural camera and focal plane, keeping the ring centered.

fixes.problem: in-scene (in-model) logo renders the whole logo in GOLD, recoloring the tagline 'FUTURE OF FINE JEWELRY' to gold. On the official artwork that tagline is BLACK/dark - only the diamond emblem + 'LUCENT CARAT LAB' are gold. Observed across a full catalog's studio shots.
fixes.root_cause: the diffusion model reproduces the logo as a single-color gold hot-foil and cannot reliably hold the official two-tone (gold emblem/wordmark + dark tagline).
fixes.fix: The logo is TWO-TONE and must stay exact: diamond emblem + 'LUCENT CARAT LAB' = metallic GOLD; 'FUTURE OF FINE JEWELRY' tagline = BLACK/dark (as in assets/logo/logo_official.png). NEVER recolor the tagline to gold. In-model prompts must state the tagline color explicitly; VERIFY it on every studio render. If the model still gold-ifies the tagline (it usually will), that is a logo-fidelity failure -> fall through to the exact-logo LOCAL COMPOSITE (scripts/print_logo_on_cloth.py from the pixel-exact two-tone asset), which preserves the black tagline. Exact logo color/typography > in-model convenience.

fixes.problem: studio logo either (a) missing because the shot was left on clean cloth, or (b) present but looking like a flat vector sticker floating on the cloth - ignoring folds, razor-crisp, no weave showing through, own lighting, no embed. USER MANDATE (2026-07-12): the Lucent Carat Lab logo is a REQUIRED part of every studio scene, physically printed on the white fabric beneath the ring; never remove/fade/blur/crop/replace it.
fixes.root_cause: clean-cloth-only shots drop a required element; naive in-model logos come out as flat overlays because a diffusion model tends to draw a clean vector on top instead of a print integrated into the weave.
fixes.observed_failure_2026-07-16: studio render shipped a logo that reads as a DIGITAL OVERLAY: logo sharper than the softer cloth; gold lines on top of the weave with no fabric grain showing through; no fold deformation (stayed flat); no ink sink into fibres; uniform self-lighting not matching the cloth's light direction; not partly hidden by highlights/valleys. = watermark look. INVALID.
fixes.hard_rule: LOGO MUST NEVER APPEAR AS A DIGITAL OVERLAY. It must be physically printed on the cloth BEFORE the photo. FORBIDDEN (any one = reject): background plate, white patch, shadow behind logo, glow, outline, opacity tricks, compositing/watermark appearance, post-production-placement look. REQUIRED: follows the cloth weave; warps with every fold; stretches with the fabric; receives IDENTICAL lighting as the cloth (no independent brightness); loses sharpness with camera focus/DoF (never sharper than the cloth); partly hidden by folds/highlights/valleys where applicable; ink slightly sinks into the fibres like real metallic fabric printing. If the logo looks digitally placed, REJECT the image and regenerate in-scene or fall back to scripts/print_logo_on_cloth.py. Never ship an overlay-looking logo.
fixes.fix: PRIMARY (mandated): generate the studio shot WITH the logo IN-SCENE. Feed the model both the official logo artwork (assets/logo/logo_official.png -> media) AND a branded-cloth reference, and instruct: reproduce the EXACT logo as premium metallic GOLD HOT-FOIL STAMPING printed into the white fabric beneath the ring. The foil MUST: follow every cloth fold/wrinkle/curve; let the fabric weave stay visible through it; inherit the cloth's exact lighting/shadows/highlights; stay sharp, centered, fully visible, at the SAME SCALE as the reference; preserve the exact design/proportions/spacing/typography (LUCENT CARAT LAB / FUTURE OF FINE JEWELRY). It must NOT float, overlay, emboss, engrave, sit on a separate layer, or look like a digital graphic - it looks permanently printed into the cloth. VERIFY every render vs the official artwork; if the logo typography/design is wrong, or it floats/embosses, REJECT and regenerate - do NOT remove or ship it altered. Missing logo = INVALID. FALLBACK (only if in-model cannot reproduce the exact logo after retries): composite the locked logo locally via scripts/print_logo_on_cloth.py (0 credits, pixel-exact; enforces fold displacement, soft edges, weave-through, darken-only edge absorption, brightness-clamped matched lighting, ink-diffusion grain, flat hot-foil finish). Either path must end with the exact logo permanently printed into the fabric.

fixes.problem: credits/tokens wasted on throwaway artifacts: preview images, draft renders, thumbnails, comparison collages, intermediate/work-in-progress outputs, low-quality test images, or preview versions made 'for confirmation'; regenerations that accumulate multiple preview copies of the same shot instead of replacing; extra images beyond the requested count; verbose reasoning / repeated image analysis / preview widgets.
fixes.root_cause: generating anything other than the final full-quality deliverable burns credits and tokens with zero delivery value.
fixes.fix: GENERATE ONLY FINAL FULL-QUALITY OUTPUT (user-locked 2026-07-16). Never generate previews/drafts/thumbnails/collages/intermediate/WIP/low-quality-test images; never display intermediate processing results; never create a preview version for confirmation. If a shot must be redone, REPLACE the previous image - do not produce multiple preview versions. Generate EXACTLY the number of final images requested - no extras. Minimize API calls, image uploads, logging, repeated image analysis, and verbose reasoning; think internally; return only the final completed output ready for review. NO conflict with the 'ONE verification image, then batch' step: that single image is a full-quality 2K FINAL (first of the requested set, counts toward the total), not a draft/preview - this rule forbids only extra/quality-reduced/throwaway renders. Preview widgets show_generations/job_display remain BANNED (docs/05).

fixes.problem: unclear when to ask for approval: asking per image wastes turns/credits, while auto-batching before the user has approved the look ships a whole catalog off a wrong standard.
fixes.root_cause: no single locked gate defining exactly one approval per catalog and freezing the approved image as the master standard.
fixes.fix: CATALOG APPROVAL WORKFLOW (user-locked 2026-07-16). Each catalog (new SKU/source ring) is independent. STEP 1: generate ONLY Image 1; collect every correction; regenerate Image 1; repeat until the user EXPLICITLY approves it; generate nothing else for the catalog until then. STEP 2 (LOCK): treat approved Image 1 as the MASTER QUALITY STANDARD and freeze jewelry geometry, diamond size/orientation/position, stone count, stone shape, prongs, halo, gallery, band width, metal thickness, camera quality, lighting, cloth, logo placement, logo print quality, QC rules for the rest of the catalog. STEP 3: AUTOMATICALLY generate all remaining images in one run - do not stop after each, do not re-ask approval unless a CRITICAL error is detected, apply every correction learned from Image 1, never repeat a corrected mistake. STEP 4: a different design/SKU RESETS the workflow (Image 1 -> approve -> auto-batch the rest). MANDATORY: exactly ONE approval image per catalog; never require approval per image; never generate the remaining catalog before Image 1 is approved; approved Image 1 is the permanent reference standard for every remaining image. Consistent with CLAUDE_SETUP 2.5/5 and docs/05 preview-optimization: the verification/approval image is a full-quality final, not a draft.

fixes.problem: quality can silently degrade: a change to the prompt/pipeline/compositing/logo/QC improves one thing but regresses fidelity, realism, or consistency vs a previously approved output, and ships unnoticed.
fixes.root_cause: no fixed baseline + regression suite, and multiple variables changed at once, so a degradation is neither detected nor attributable.
fixes.fix: NO-REGRESSION POLICY (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/14). Quality only ratchets UP. (1) NEVER REGRESS: the last approved pipeline+config is the baseline; every change runs the golden regression suite and is compared to the previous version; if even one critical metric gets worse, reject + roll back. (2) PASS/FAIL METRICS before delivery - ring geometry/stone shape/orientation/size/metal thickness are GUARANTEED by composite provenance (real source pixels); ring worn-scale, logo-printed, cloth realism, lighting consistency, no-AI-artifacts are verified per-shot/approval; any fail = do NOT deliver. (3) ONE CHANGE AT A TIME: never modify prompt+pipeline+preprocessing+compositing+logo+masking+QC together; change one, test, keep only if it improves and regresses nothing. (4) GOLDEN CATALOG: permanent regression set (halo, solitaire, infinity/twist, emerald eternity, pave, three-stone, hidden halo x yellow/white/rose gold; 10-20 SKUs) in config/golden_catalog.json + workspace/golden/ (operator-provided, never fabricated); harness lib/pipeline/regression.py runs the pipeline over all. (5) ROLLBACK on success-rate drop: revert + restore previous config + investigate in isolation; revert is a GATED human/agent step, never an autonomous git history rewrite; main always holds the last non-regressing version. (6) quality-first per-catalog approval unchanged (catalog-approval-workflow). (7) main always runnable (clone -> .env -> setup -> start).

fixes.problem: any AI regeneration of the jewelry (even one pixel) risks redesigning/inventing/altering geometry - the recurring failure across 6 SKUs.
fixes.root_cause: prompt-based generation re-synthesizes the ring; the only guarantee is to never let AI touch jewelry pixels at all.
fixes.fix: JEWELRY PRESERVATION RULE (ABSOLUTE, HIGHEST PRIORITY, user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/02). ZERO AI generation on the jewelry: not a single pixel may be recreated/redesigned/repainted/re-rendered/hallucinated/enhanced/repaired/cleaned/sharpened/upscaled/modified. Covers center+side stones, halo, hidden halo, gallery, basket, prongs, head, cathedral, bridge, shank, band, pave, channel, bezel, metal thickness, curves, profile, underside, open gallery, stone orientation, facets, stone count/size/spacing, metal color, finish, reflections, engraving. AI may generate ONLY the environment (background, room, furniture, cloth, hand, skin, nails, person, hair, lighting, shadows-except-behind-logo, reflection environment, camera, DoF/bokeh) - everything EXCEPT the jewelry; the jewelry is TRANSFERRED unaltered. JEWELRY = LOCKED READ-ONLY ASSET, same protection as the P0 logo/watermark: AI owns the scene only; the source owns 100% of the jewelry; it is NOT an AI generation target. ONLY whole-asset non-destructive ops allowed: preserve, position, scale uniformly, rotate as a whole, perspective-transform as a whole - NEVER rebuild/rasterize/redraw/repaint/inpaint/diffuse/re-render/regenerate at the pixel level. If a processing step would modify the jewelry, SKIP it or fail safely - never alter. Priority: (1) preserve jewelry exactly (highest); (2) generate environment; (3) blend without changing any jewelry pixel. FAIL-CLOSED: if the jewelry cannot be preserved exactly (e.g. an angle the source cannot supply), STOP - report the angle cannot be produced, request more source (CAD angle / 3D model), never invent; failure is preferred over reconstruction. Any modification = rejected automatically. Founding principle of composite-v1 (ring = source pixels -> guaranteed by construction); legacy must pass the difference detector (docs/16) or fail. Umbrella over geometry-immutable-auto-fallback, zero-jewelry-invention, and the head/gallery lock.

fixes.problem: need one pipeline policy that guarantees 100% jewelry geometry across a full catalog. Composite-v1 from 2D CAD guarantees studio geometry but cannot faithfully produce worn lifestyle/closeup shots (top-down CAD onto an angled finger = pasted); legacy AI redraws the ring (violates jewelry preservation).
fixes.root_cause: 2D CAD renders lack worn-angle coverage; only a 3D CAD model (render the worn angle) or a real worn photo can keep lifestyle geometry-perfect.
fixes.fix: HYBRID POLICY, composite-v1 = DEFAULT (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/15). Geometry is the highest priority (docs/02). STUDIO: always composite (AI never regenerates jewelry/logo). LIFESTYLE/CLOSEUP: composite whenever the worn angle is achievable from source; if not achievable faithfully, (1) composite the preserved jewelry, else (2) REQUEST more source (more CAD angles / a 3D model -> FALLBACK 2 render, docs/13 6), else (3) SKIP the shot. NEVER auto-run legacy / never let AI redraw the jewelry - missing an image is preferable to a geometrically incorrect product. Legacy retained for MANUAL experimentation only (one-command switch), never automatic, never a fallback (both fallback_to=null; dispatch sets action_required + skips instead). Every output must pass automatic geometry QC before delivery. Modular: pipeline chosen by one value (env PIPELINE_MODE / registry active); all prompts/QC/learning reusable across pipelines; validated learning kept separate from implementation (docs/15 6-7). Do NOT switch the default away from composite-v1 without explicit instruction.

fixes.problem: a composite preserved geometry perfectly (ring = source pixels) but was still a FAILED image: composited onto a scene that already had a ring (double ring / original halo peeking behind the inserted solitaire), with the source drop-shadow left un-keyed as a white mask/segmentation-residue patch, and mismatched contact lighting. qc_final false-PASSED it on geometry provenance alone.
fixes.root_cause: geometry provenance != deliverable. The failure came from a DIRTY (ring-bearing) scene + loose keying; QC only checked that ring pixels were from source, not composite integration.
fixes.fix: COMPOSITE INTEGRITY (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/16). Checks (reject if any fail): original_object_removed, single_ring_present, no_segmentation_artifacts, no_white_mask_residue, consistent_lighting_shadows, natural_background_integration. Guarantee at the INPUT: composite ONLY into a clean ring-free scene (empty cloth / bare finger) and key the source with a clean alpha (drop its shadow). qc.composite_integrity HARD-FAILS original_object_removed + single_ring_present unless caller asserts scene_is_clean=True; segmentation/residue/lighting/integration are vision/manual 'unverified' (classical CV can't reliably detect a soft white-mask patch - reads like cloth highlights; no pixel-detector claimed). qc_final no longer auto-passes a composite on geometry alone: stays geometry_guaranteed but passed=False until integrity satisfied. Geometry regression suite asserts geometry_guaranteed only; integrity checked per-shot/shadow-test.

fixes.problem: displaying/opening images in chat during processing (to 'verify' visually, or as thumbnails/markdown previews) burns tokens, bloats context, and slows the conversation.
fixes.root_cause: rendering images in chat is unnecessary for processing — inspection can be done in code and reported as text.
fixes.fix: NO IMAGE PREVIEW MODE (default, user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/05). Never display generated/downloaded images, never open/Read an image to verify it visually, never embed thumbnails/previews, never send image markdown. If an image must be inspected, do it IN CODE (dimensions, checksums, the jewelry difference detector) and return TEXT ONLY (e.g. checkmark lines: downloaded / resolution / format / geometry check passed / ready, or a failure reason). Show images ONLY when the user types 'preview', 'show image', or 'compare images', or at final approved catalog delivery. Complements preview-optimization (don't generate throwaway previews); this is about not DISPLAYING images. QC still runs via code, returning text.

fixes.problem: raw AI render INVENTS jewelry components absent from the source: added a pavé/diamond bridge + gallery diamonds beneath the center stone, redesigned the open cathedral basket, changed prong shape/angle/thickness, altered basket height + head-to-shank relation, flattened/widened the center stone. Source had a plain open basket with no accent row. Invention subtype of geometry drift.
fixes.root_cause: the diffusion model adds statistically-common luxury details (hidden halo, pave bridge, gallery diamonds) that the prompt does not forbid explicitly; generation invents where the source is plain.
fixes.fix: ZERO JEWELRY INVENTION POLICY (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/16). NEVER add/remove/modify any component not in the source: no added accent diamonds, hidden halo, pave/diamond bridge, gallery/surprise diamonds, extra prongs/galleries, added metal supports, filigree, split shank, cathedral conversion, basket redesign, or stone-count change. If a feature is not visible in the source, DO NOT create it - missing stays missing; never improve/add luxury details. Only environment/lighting/camera/perspective/hand/DoF/shadows/reflections may change. GATE: the JEWELRY DIFFERENCE DETECTOR (lib/pipeline/qc.jewelry_difference_detector, folded into qc_final) checks render-vs-source for diamond_count, diamond_locations, gallery_structure, prong_count, hidden_halo_presence, pave_bridge_presence, metal_silhouette; ANY difference = auto-reject before delivery. HEAD & GALLERY GEOMETRY LOCK (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/16): the center-stone assembly is inspected SEPARATELY (HEAD_GEOMETRY_CHECKS -> head:* keys): prong_count/thickness/angle/position, basket_shape, gallery_shape, bridge_geometry, under_gallery, head_height/width/thickness, metal_volume, no_added_support_ring, no_added_gallery_rail, no_extra_bridge. Observed failure: raw render added a thick circular support ring below the center stone + reshaped the gallery + thicker head + more metal volume (source had a plain open basket). Never add a support ring/girdle rail/gallery rail/metal collar/extra bridge/thicker head/any structural metal absent from source; if metal appears that is not in the source, fail QC automatically. Composite render (composite-v1) = invention IMPOSSIBLE (ring is source pixels), auto-pass - the reliable fix. Raw render (legacy) = needs a vision diff (Claude vision in-session or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); until run it is UNVERIFIED and must NOT be auto-accepted (classical CV cannot count stones/spot a bridge - never fabricate a pass).

fixes.problem: a new pipeline could silently replace the working one, a rollback could lose validated learning, or an unproven change could become default before proving equal-or-better.
fixes.root_cause: no versioned pipelines, no one-value switch, no shadow-test gate, and learning tied to pipeline implementation.
fixes.fix: SAFE PIPELINE VERSIONING + ZERO-LOSS LEARNING (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/15). (1) PRESERVE: git tag pipeline-stable marks last proven commit; config/pipeline_versions.json snapshots each version's prompt/provider/QC/geometry/compositing profile; legacy stays runnable, never deleted. (2) VERSIONED: legacy (stable default, prompt-based) + composite-v1 (experimental, geometry guaranteed by compositing real source pixels); select via ONE value (env PIPELINE_MODE overrides registry active) - resolver lib/pipeline/mode.py; no source edits. (3) ROLLBACK: scripts/rollback-pipeline.ps1|.sh <mode> restores that version's profile + verifies imports. (4) SHADOW TEST before replacement (dispatch.shadow_test, POST /shadow-test): geometry categories auto-decided (composite guaranteed vs legacy unverified), scene categories = needs_human; promote composite-v1 to stable ONLY when equal-or-better in EVERY critical fidelity category. (5) AUTO-FALLBACK (dispatch.generate, POST /generate): run selected pipeline -> QC -> on failure fall back once (single hop) to the version's fallback_to. Bidirectional: legacy->composite-v1 (raw render failing geometry gate is rescued by compositing the real ring) and composite-v1->legacy (if composite cannot produce a valid image, fall back to the STABLE pipeline; that legacy render is geometry-unverified so it routes to the human approval gate, never auto-shipped). Record which pipeline delivered; never deliver below the approved baseline. (6) LEARNING separate from code: QUALITY_MEMORY.json = validated shared store (both pipelines read); config/learning_candidates.json = candidate store; rolling back code never deletes validated learning. (7) PROMOTION: candidate -> validated only after it improves output or user approves; a bad candidate is disabled WITH failure evidence, never deleted. (8) APPROVED BASELINE per SKU in config/deliveries/LR-XXXX.json (source, approved first image, pipeline version, prompt hash, provider/model/seed, geometry+camera/lighting/cloth/logo profiles, corrections, QC report); never deliver below it. (9) GIT SAFETY: main stays stable; risky work isolated by the PIPELINE_MODE flag + versioned modules (not branches); before promotion commit+tag+regression+test-rollback+verify-both+push. (10) improvements reversible, validated learning permanent, failed experiments recorded not repeated, stable pipeline always available.
